title: How much to trust the new

data.source: A drifting hidden level seen through noise (the local level model), thousands of seeded runs.

prediction: In a steady world the seed rule with q = 1 - K* matches the Kalman filter; from a fresh start, and when the quality of observations changes, a fixed q does worse, because the precision-weighted update changes its gain and the seed rule cannot.
baseline: The Kalman filter, which is the exact Bayes update here and the linear form of precision-weighted predictive coding.
why: All four predictions held. The seed rule is the fixed-gain special case of the precision-weighted update: equal to it in a steady world, weaker when trust should change, and silent on what q should be.
